title: Local equational criterion for flatness of module sheaves
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $A$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and let $M$ be a sheaf of $A$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then $M$ is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] if and only if the following holds: for every object $U$, integer $n\geq0$, and sections $a_1,\ldots,a_n\in A(U)$ and $s_1,\ldots,s_n\in M(U)$ with $\sum_{p=1}^n a_p s_p=0$, there is a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ and, for each $i$, an integer $l_i\geq0$, sections $b_{ipq}\in A(U_i)$ and $t_{iq}\in M(U_i)$ ($1\leq p\leq n$, $1\leq q\leq l_i$), such that $s_p|_{U_i}=\sum_q b_{ipq}t_{iq}$ for every $p$ and $\sum_p a_p|_{U_i}b_{ipq}=0$ for every $q$.

proof.text: For a flat M, tensoring any presheaf monomorphism with M and then sheafifying is monic. Indeed module sheafification is left exact and monoidal. Its tensor comparison and the counit isomorphism for M identify this composite with sheafification followed by tensorRight M. The latter preserves monomorphisms by flatness. This is tensor_presheaf_mono in Lean.

source.place: Tag 08FC, (1) implies (2); monoidal sheafification and exactness

proof.text: First suppose the coefficients a_p form a natural family on the entire site. Form the presheaf ideal I whose sections are the span of the a_p. The tensor z = sum a_p tensor s_p in I tensor M maps to zero in A tensor M by the given relation. The preceding monomorphism implies its image in the associated sheaf is zero. Mathlib Presheaf.equalizerSieve_mem for the locally injective sheafification unit produces a covering sieve on which z already vanishes. On each member the a_p generate I, so Mathlib TensorProduct.vanishesTrivially_of_sum_tmul_eq_zero produces finite b_pq and t_q, with s_p = sum b_pq t_q and sum b_pq a_p = 0 in I and hence in A. These constructions include empty finite families.

source.place: Tag 08FC, ideal proof of (1) implies (2); Algebra Tag 04VX, finite generators and vanishing tensors

proof.text: For coefficients given over U, pass to the slice site C/U. The restrictions of a_p are natural on that site. Restriction of M is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-slice-restriction-flat], so the previous step applies at the terminal object. Mathlib Sieve.overEquiv identifies its covering sieve with one over U, and Precoverage.mem_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderComposition supplies a presieve in J contained in it. Read the factorization there. Only the existing same-universe over and monoidal APIs are used.

source.place: Tag 08FC, reduction to global coefficients on C/U

proof.text: Conversely induct on the number m of simultaneous coefficient relations. For m = 0 take the identity cover, the original sections, and the identity matrix. At m+1 first factor the last relation by the assumed single-relation criterion. Substitute this factorization into the other m relations, apply induction on each member of that cover, and multiply the two coefficient matrices. Distributivity and commutativity show that all original relations vanish on the resulting columns. Compose the presieve coverings using Precoverage.comp_mem_coverings. This is local_matrix in Lean.

A tensor z in G tensor T killed by j tensor 1 has finite witnesses: choose a finite sum expression for z, lift it to G tensor R[T], and use right exactness for ker(epsilon) -> R[T] -> T. A finite sum expression for the resulting element of H tensor ker(epsilon), together with the finite supports of its free-module coordinates and the original summands, gives g_p, s_p, d_pk, h_k with z = sum g_p tensor s_p, sum d_pk s_p = 0, and j(g_p) = sum d_pk h_k. This is the proved finite_tensor_relation helper. Apply it sectionwise to a presheaf monomorphism P -> Q. The matrix criterion factors the s_p locally. Naturality and injectivity of P(V) -> Q(V) show sum b_pq g_p|V = 0, so the restricted tensor is zero by bilinearity (Mathlib TensorProduct.sum_tmul_eq_zero_of_vanishesTrivially).

source.place: Tag 08FC, (3) implies (1), finite-generators/finite-relations reduction; Algebra Tag 00HA

proof.text: Apply the preceding local-kernel calculation to x-y to see that the sectionwise tensor of any monomorphism of module sheaves is locally injective. Mathlib Presheaf.isLocallyInjective_presheafToSheaf_map_iff and Sheaf.mono_of_isLocallyInjective imply that its associated-sheaf map is monic. The natural tensorObjIsoSheafification comparisons identify this map with tensorRight M applied to the original monomorphism. The existing closed symmetric monoidal structure makes tensorRight M a left adjoint and hence preserves colimits; MonoidalFree supplies additivity. Mathlib Functor.preservesHomology_of_preservesMonos_and_cokernels and preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesHomology now give preservation of finite limits. Together with finite colimits this is IsFlat M.

source.place: Tag 08FC, conclusion of (3) implies (1); existing closed monoidal and exact-functor APIs
